Messages.Author: prunesquallor
Messages.Body:
The original Jyhad set had quite a few misprints like this. It was 1994, WotC was moving as fast as they could to capitalize on the success of MtG and get another game out, and lots of mistakes were made.

Blood Rage was a misprint, and was intended to be a Thaumaturgy card from the beginning. Some of them, like this one, they admitted to the mistake.

Then there is Concealed Weapon, which was pretty obviously intended to be a disciplineless card but was printed as Obfuscate, and which never received an errata until the card was reprinted with slightly different text. And I've heard the theory that Sport Bike was intended to give the maneuver while IR Goggles was intended to give the Intercept. And then there are all the issues with copied artwork, use of song quotes in flavor text that didn't have copyright, etc...

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> AaronC wrote:
> I read somewhere that the disciplines of Appolonius and Anvil got switched.
>
As far as I know, no-one from Wizards has ever acknowledged this. However, if you look at the "points" system that - roughly speaking - appears to have been used for other Jyhad vampires, if you switch the capacities over, the two vampires are close. If Anvil had two superiors, two inferiors, and no title, he'd fit 6 points under the Jyhad "system". Badger is a vampire with a similar setup.

7 points of disciplines, +1 bleed (2-ish points), title (maybe 1 point, maybe 0.5/vote, depends who you ask), and a press can get you to 10-11 points fairly easily. If Appolonius had tha (which Anvil does), a press might well have been considered reasonably valuable. (Certainly, it was considered way more valuable than we'd generally regard it as today.)

> AaronC wrote:
> I've often thought that IR Goggles and Sports Bike do what the other should; now I know it might be because of a production error.
>
Hard to say, really. Some intercept abilities are reasonably longer range, like KRCG News Radio, Mr Winthrop, or Raven Spy. It's entirely plausible that a Sport Bike represented being able to catch up with someone.
